mainTopic: The Torah sources for when בִּיעוּר חָמֵץ begins: midday on the 14th of ניסן
overview: This amud is about when the duty to remove חמץ begins. It opens by finishing an answer: the night of the 15th needs no extra source, because a chain of הֶקֵּשׁ links removal to the איסור of eating חמץ, and that איסור to eating מצה, which starts that night. The גמרא then shows that removal does not start on the night of the 14th, because the פסוק says בַּיּוֹם. It also does not start in the morning, because אַךְ splits the day, so removal begins at midday. Next, דבי רבי ישמעאל and רב נחמן בר יצחק show that ראשון can mean the 14th, the day before the חג. The גמרא challenges this from several verses, mostly about סוכות, where ראשון clearly means the first day of the חג, and tries answers based on the seven-day count, the eighth day, and the extra ה. In the end it says those three ראשון are written for a lesson about reward: wiping out עשו, building the בית המקדש, and the name of משיח. רבא then gives a separate source: do not slaughter the קרבן פסח while חמץ still exists. A ברייתא supports this and adds two more proofs, from רבי עקיבא (no burning on יום טוב) and רבי יוסי (אַךְ divides the day). The amud ends with the גמרא questioning how anyone could think חמץ is allowed on יום טוב, and רבא's answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: Removal is linked to eating חמץ, and eating חמץ is linked to מצה
steps.stepSummary: The night of the 15th needs no extra source, because השבתת שאור is linked to אכילת חמץ, and אכילת חמץ is linked to אכילת מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For removing leaven is compared to eating חמץ, and eating חמץ is compared to eating מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to the earlier question. That question asked whether an extra word is needed to include the night of the 15th in the duty of removing חמץ. The answer is that it is not needed, because a chain of two comparisons already covers that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Link 1: the duty to remove חמץ applies whenever eating חמץ is forbidden. Link 2: eating חמץ is forbidden whenever the מצוה of eating מצה applies, and that מצוה begins on the night of the 15th. So the duty of removal already applies on the night of the 15th, and the word אַךְ is free for a different purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: It was compared (linked) through a הֶקֵּשׁ, meaning the two topics appear together in the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new topic. It is the end of an answer to a question asked on the previous amud, about whether the night of the 15th needs its own source.

phrases.english: For the removal of leaven is compared
phrases.notes: דְּהָא means 'for, after all'; it's bringing a reason.

phrases.english: to the eating of חמץ,
and the eating of חמץ is compared to the eating of מצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question asked on the previous amud, about including the night of the 15th
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The night of the 15th is already covered by a two-step הֶקֵּשׁ, so no extra word is needed for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the word אַךְ is free for another purpose. That frees the גמרא to raise the next question about the night of the 14th.

steps.title: Source for linking removal to eating חמץ
steps.stepSummary: Both topics appear in one פסוק: 'leaven shall not be found in your houses' and 'whoever eats חמץ gets כרת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Removing leaven is compared to eating חמץ, as it is written: "For seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses, for whoever eats leavened food will be cut off."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves the first link in the chain by quoting the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק speaks about not having חמץ in the house (removal) and about the punishment for eating חמץ. Because the Torah puts them side by side, they are linked. Wherever eating חמץ is forbidden, removal is required.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall not be found, meaning you may not own חמץ
Will be cut off, which is the punishment of כָּרֵת

phrases.english: Removal of leaven is compared to eating חמץ,
as it is written: "Seven days
leaven shall not be found in your houses,
for whoever eats leavened food will be cut off."
phrases.notes: שמות יב:יט

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first link of the chain stated in step 1
steps.raayaObject: That removing leaven is linked to the איסור of eating חמץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות יב:יט, where both ideas appear in one פסוק

steps.title: Source for linking eating חמץ to eating מצה
steps.stepSummary: Eating חמץ and eating מצה appear in one פסוק, and the מצוה of מצה is stated for the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Eating חמץ is compared to eating מצה, as it is written: "You shall not eat anything leavened; in all your dwellings you shall eat מצות." And it is written about מצה: "In the evening you shall eat מצות."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second link of the chain. It also shows that the מצוה of מצה starts in the evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק places the איסור of חמץ right next to eating מצה, so the two are linked. A different פסוק says מצה is eaten 'in the evening', which is the night of the 15th. So the איסור of חמץ, and with it the duty of removal, is in force that night as well.

keyTerms.meaning: In the evening, meaning the night of the 15th

steps.whatToRemember: The chain works like this: removal is linked to eating חמץ, eating חמץ is linked to eating מצה, and eating מצה starts at night. So removal applies on the night of the 15th without any extra word.

phrases.english: And eating חמץ is compared to eating מצה,
as it is written: "You shall not eat anything leavened;
in all your dwellings you shall eat מצות (etc.)"
phrases.notes: שמות יב:כ

phrases.english: and it is written regarding מצה:
"In the evening you shall eat מצות."
phrases.notes: שמות יב:יח

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second link of the chain and completes the answer
steps.raayaObject: That the איסור of eating חמץ is linked to the מצוה of מצה, which begins at night
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות יב:כ together with שמות יב:יח

steps.title: Maybe the extra word includes the night of the 14th
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the extra word might add the night of the 14th to the duty of removing חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead that it comes to include the night of the 14th for removal?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the extra word is free, the גמרא suggests a new job for it: requiring removal of חמץ already on the night of the 14th. This sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the night of the 15th is already covered, perhaps the extra word stretches the duty of removal earlier, to the night before ערב פסח. If so, the time for removal would start at night instead of during the day on the 14th.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead, which introduces an alternative reading
To include, meaning to add a case
The night of the 14th of ניסן

phrases.english: But say it comes to include
the night of the 14th for removal?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא לְרַבּוֹת לֵיל אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר לְבִיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the extra word is now free, the גמרא proposes a different use for it
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that removal begins only during the daytime of the 14th
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unused extra word could extend the duty of removal back to the night of the 14th.

steps.title: The פסוק says "day", so night is excluded
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says בַּיּוֹם, which means daytime, so the night of the 14th cannot be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: "On the day" is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion with two words. The פסוק itself says 'on the day'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reads "אַךְ בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן תַּשְׁבִּיתוּ". The word בַּיּוֹם clearly limits the duty of removal to daytime. So the extra word cannot be read as adding the night of the 14th.

keyTerms.meaning: On the day, meaning daytime and not night

steps.whatToRemember: Removal of חמץ does not start on the night of the 14th, because the פסוק says 'day'. The night of the 15th is covered by the הֶקֵּשׁ chain.

phrases.english: "On the day" is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual limitation: the word in the פסוק excludes the proposed case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra word might add the night of the 14th to the duty of removal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word בַּיּוֹם limits removal to daytime, so the night of the 14th is excluded.

steps.title: Maybe removing חמץ starts from the morning of the 14th
steps.stepSummary: Since the night is excluded, perhaps the duty of removing חמץ starts at daybreak on the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say it starts from the morning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the night of the 14th is excluded. It now asks why the duty would not start right at the morning of the 14th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said בַּיּוֹם means daytime. The simple meaning of 'day' is the whole day, so the duty to remove חמץ should start at sunrise. The challenge asks what pushes the start time later.

phrases.english: And say from the morning!
phrases.notes: From the morning of the 14th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 5 and pushes further: if daytime counts, why not the whole day?
steps.kashyaTarget: The start time of the duty to remove חמץ on the 14th
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בַּיּוֹם plainly means the whole day, so the duty should begin at sunrise.

steps.title: The word אך splits the day
steps.stepSummary: The word אך limits the day, so removing חמץ applies only to the second half of the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'אך' divides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word אך in the פסוק cuts the day in half. Only the afternoon of the 14th is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אך is a limiting word. Here it tells us that not all of the day is included, only part of it. So the duty to remove חמץ begins at midday.
steps.whatToRemember: The duty to remove חמץ starts at midday of the 14th: ביום excludes the night, and אך excludes the morning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the Torah source that חמץ becomes forbidden from חצות on ערב פסח.

phrases.english: 'Yet' divides.
phrases.notes: From the פסוק 'אַךְ בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן תַּשְׁבִּיתוּ שְּׂאֹר'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Removing חמץ applies from the morning of the 14th.
steps.terutzMaskana: אך limits it to the second half of the day only.

steps.title: דבי רבי ישמעאל: the 14th is called 'first'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows from a פסוק that the 14th of ניסן is called ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: We found that the 14th is called 'first', as it says: 'In the first, on the fourteenth day of the month'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source showing that ראשון in 'ביום הראשון תשביתו' can mean the 14th. A פסוק calls the 14th 'ראשון'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in שמות says 'בראשון בארבעה עשר', which links the word ראשון directly to the 14th. So when the פסוק says 'ביום הראשון תשביתו שאור', it can mean the 14th, not the first day of the חג.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study hall) of רבי ישמעאל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ראשון here means the first day of פסח (the 15th). The point is that ראשון refers to the 14th, the day before the חג.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
We have found the fourteenth called 'first',
as it is said: 'In the first, on the fourteenth day of the month'.
phrases.notes: שמות יב:יח

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a separate source showing that ראשון means the 14th.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah calls the 14th of ניסן 'ראשון'.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: ראשון means 'earlier'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves from איוב that ראשון can mean 'before', so it can mean the day before the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: 'First' means 'earlier', as the פסוק says: 'Were you born before (first of) man?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives his own proof. He shows that the word ראשון itself can mean 'earlier'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In איוב, 'הראשון אדם תולד' means 'were you born before Adam?' So ראשון can mean 'the one before'. In our פסוק, 'היום הראשון' then means the day before the חג, the 14th.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
'First' means 'earlier',
as the verse says: 'Were you born before man?'
phrases.notes: איוב טו:ז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different source for the same idea as step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That ראשון can mean 'earlier', so the day before the חג

steps.title: Challenge from the ארבעה מינים on סוכות
steps.stepSummary: If ראשון means 'earlier', then 'ביום הראשון' for the ארבעה מינים would mean the 14th of תשרי, which is clearly wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, 'And you shall take for yourselves on the first day': there too does 'first' mean 'earlier'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן בר יצחק's rule. It uses the פסוק about taking the ארבעה מינים on סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words 'ביום הראשון' appear for סוכות. If ראשון always means 'earlier', we would take the לולב on ערב סוכות, which nobody holds. So the rule seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall take for yourselves (the ארבעה מינים)

phrases.english: But if so,
'And you shall take for yourselves on the first day',
phrases.notes: ויקרא כג:מ

phrases.english: so too does 'first' mean 'earlier'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's rule that ראשון means 'earlier'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applied to סוכות, the rule would move the לולב to the 14th of תשרי, which is clearly wrong.

steps.title: סוכות is different because seven days are counted
steps.stepSummary: On סוכות the פסוק counts seven days of the חג, so ראשון there means the first day of the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written: 'And you shall rejoice before ה׳ your God seven days.' Just as 'seventh' is the seventh of the חג, so 'first' is the first of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that סוכות has a special reason in its own פסוק. There, ראשון must mean the first day of the חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק counts seven days of the חג. The seventh day is surely a day of the חג, so the 'first' in that count must also be a day of the חג. Where there is no such count, as with חמץ, ראשון keeps its meaning of 'earlier'.
steps.whatToRemember: ראשון normally means 'earlier', so for חמץ it means the 14th. On סוכות it means the first day of the חג only because that פסוק counts seven days.

phrases.english: It is different there, as it is written:
'And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days',
just as 'seventh' is the seventh of the festival,
so too 'first' is the first of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case by context (שאני התם)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If ראשון means 'earlier', the לולב would be taken on ערב סוכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: On סוכות, the counting of seven days of the חג makes ראשון mean the first day of the חג. Elsewhere it means 'earlier'.

steps.title: פסח Also Counts Seven Days
steps.stepSummary: The answer from סוכות (a count of seven days means ראשון is the first day of the חג) should apply to פסח too, since פסח also mentions seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, by פסח, it is written: 'Yet on the first day you shall remove leaven… for seven days you shall eat מצות'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading that ראשון means the 14th of ניסן. The same verse about פסח also counts seven days, just like סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the גמרא said that on סוכות, a count of seven days makes ראשון mean day one of the חג. The very same verse that says 'תשביתו' also says 'שבעת ימים מצות תאכלו'. So by the same logic, ראשון by פסח should mean the 15th. That would knock out the proof that חמץ must be removed on the 14th.

phrases.english: Here too it is written:
"Yet on the first day you shall remove (leaven)
phrases.notes: שמות יב:טו

phrases.english: for seven days you shall eat matzos"!
phrases.notes: The same count of seven days as by סוכות

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 11 against the פסח derivation
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that הראשון by פסח means the 14th (steps 8-9)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If counting seven days makes ראשון mean first of the חג on סוכות, the same count on פסח should do the same.

steps.title: The Extra Letter ה Shows 'Earlier'
steps.stepSummary: The verse could have written just ראשון. Writing הראשון, with an extra ה, teaches that it means the day before the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse write 'ראשון'. Why do I need 'הראשון'? Learn from it what we said: it means the day before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra ה in הראשון is a clue. It tells us this ראשון means the earlier day, the 14th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the ה, the count of seven days would indeed make it mean the 15th. The extra letter is seen as unnecessary. It is therefore read as teaching the meaning 'before', which keeps the conclusion that חמץ is removed on the 14th.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need it? (this seems extra)

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write "first";
why do I need "the first"?
phrases.notes: He's asking about the extra letter ה in הָרִאשׁוֹן.

phrases.english: Learn from it as we said.
phrases.notes: Meaning the day before the חג

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seven-day count should make ראשון mean the first day of פסח
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra ה in הראשון shows it means the earlier day, the 14th

steps.title: סוכות Also Says הראשון
steps.stepSummary: If the ה means 'earlier', then by סוכות the verse also says הראשון. So why is it there?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there too (by סוכות), why do I need 'הראשון'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 13. The סוכות verse also has the ה, and there it surely does not mean 'earlier'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'an extra ה means earlier' should work in every case. On סוכות we already decided ראשון is the first day of the חג. So the ה there needs another explanation. This question stays open until step 17.

phrases.english: If so, there too,
phrases.notes: By the ארבעה מינים on סוכות

phrases.english: why do I need "the first"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13 using the סוכות verse
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the extra ה means 'earlier'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סוכות verse also has the ה, yet there it clearly means the first day of the חג. So what does the ה do there?
steps.confusionAlert: This question is not answered right away. The גמרא first adds a second question (step 15) and answers it (step 16). Only in step 17 does it come back to this one.

steps.title: Another סוכות Verse Without Seven Days
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'on the first day a שבתון and on the eighth day a שבתון' has no seven-day count. So say ראשון there means the day before.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, there it is written: 'On the first day a solemn rest and on the eighth day a solemn rest.' Say that ראשון means 'earlier'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge. A different סוכות verse has no count of seven days, so the answer of step 11 does not help there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 relied on the seven-day count. This verse about rest days does not have it. So by the logic of 'ראשון means earlier', the rest day would be the 14th of תשרי. That is clearly wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: a day of solemn rest (יום טוב)

phrases.english: And furthermore, there where it is written:
"On the first day a solemn rest
phrases.notes: ויקרא כג:לט

phrases.english: and on the eighth day a solemn rest",
say "first" means earlier?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge alongside step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from step 9 that ראשון can mean 'earlier'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This verse has no seven-day count, so nothing stops ראשון from meaning the 14th of תשרי. That is absurd.

steps.title: Eighth Proves First Is of the חג
steps.stepSummary: Because the verse says 'eighth', which is the eighth day of the חג, 'first' must also be the first day of the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says 'and on the eighth day a solemn rest'. Just as 'eighth' is the eighth of the חג, so 'first' is the first of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. The word 'eighth' next to 'first' shows we are counting days of the חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Eighth' can only mean the eighth day of the חג. Since the two are listed together, 'first' must follow the same counting. So ראשון there means the 15th, not the 14th.

phrases.english: It is different there, for the verse said:
"and on the eighth day a solemn rest";
just as "eighth" is the eighth of the festival,
so too "first" is the first of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second challenge (step 15)
steps.terutzResolutionType: Contextual comparison (the neighboring word decides the meaning)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ראשון in the rest-day verse could mean the 14th
steps.terutzMaskana: Next to 'eighth of the חג', ראשון means the first day of the חג

steps.title: The ה on סוכות Excludes חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the question of step 14. The ה of הראשון on סוכות comes to exclude חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need 'הראשון'? To exclude חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the open question from step 14 and now answers it. On סוכות the ה teaches that חול המועד is not a full שבתון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So on סוכות the extra ה has its own job and does not mean 'earlier'. That is why the rule from step 13 still stands for פסח. The ה limits the שבתון to the actual first day, not the in-between days.

keyTerms.meaning: the intermediate days of the festival

phrases.english: Why do I need "the first"?
phrases.notes: Coming back to the question of step 14

phrases.english: To exclude the intermediate days of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרִאשׁוֹן לְמָה לִי? לְמַעוֹטֵי חוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to and answers the challenge of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra letter a different purpose on סוכות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ה on סוכות has no purpose unless it means 'earlier'
steps.terutzMaskana: On סוכות the ה excludes חול המועד from the full status of שבתון

steps.title: חול המועד Is Already Excluded
steps.stepSummary: We already know חול המועד is excluded, since the verse names only the first and eighth days.
steps.simpleTranslation: חול המועד is already learned from 'first' and 'eighth'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 17. Naming only day one and day eight already shows the days in between are not שבתון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse lists only those two days as שבתון, the middle days are obviously left out. So the ה would again be extra. That would reopen the question of why it is there.

keyTerms.meaning: it is derived, it comes out from

phrases.english: The intermediate days of the festival
are derived from "first" and "eighth"!

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד מֵרִאשׁוֹן וּשְׁמִינִי נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ה is needed to exclude חול המועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Listing only the first and eighth days already excludes the middle days, so the ה is not needed for this.

steps.title: The ו Could Have Included חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The ה is needed after all. The ו in 'וביום השמיני' might have meant that the middle days are added too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought: since the Torah wrote 'and on the eighth day', and a ו adds to what came before, even חול המועד is included. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 17. Without the ה, the word 'and' (ו) might have joined everything together, including חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a ו 'adds on' to the previous matter. Here it could have suggested that the days between first and eighth are also שבתון. The extra ה blocks that mistake. So the ה on סוכות really has a purpose, and the reading of הראשון by פסח as the 14th stands.

keyTerms.meaning: the letter ו adds onto the previous matter

steps.whatToRemember: This ו-and-ה answer is only temporary. In the very next step (step 20) the גמרא asks why the Torah did not simply write neither the ו nor the ה. In step 22 it replaces this answer: the three times הראשון appears in the חג verses are needed for the teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: It was necessary:
it would enter your mind to say,
since the Merciful One wrote: "and on the eighth day",
and a vav adds onto the previous matter,
that even on the intermediate days of the festival (it applies),
so it teaches us (that it does not).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 and secures step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing the extra word is needed to block a mistaken inference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ו of 'וביום השמיני' would include חול המועד as שבתון
steps.terutzMaskana: The ה of הראשון excludes חול המועד, so it has a real purpose on סוכות

steps.title: If the ו and the ה cancel out, why write either one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks step 19. If the ו adds the middle days and the ה takes them away again, the Torah could have left out both letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let the Torah write neither the ו nor the ה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 19. If two letters simply cancel each other, why are they written at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 the ה of הראשון was needed only to undo what the ו of וביום השמיני might have added (חול המועד). But if one letter only undoes the other, leaving out both gives the same result. So this explanation of the ה does not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳ as its Author
The letter ו, here meaning 'and,' which can add something
The letter ה, here the 'the' of הראשון, which can exclude something

phrases.english: And let the Merciful One not write
neither the vav nor the heh?!
phrases.notes: If they cancel each other out, both are unnecessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא לָא וָיו וְלָא הֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ה of הראשון is needed to cancel the ו of וביום השמיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two letters that cancel each other out are pointless. The Torah could have omitted both.

steps.title: A פסח verse where ראשון cannot mean the day before
steps.stepSummary: A further challenge: about פסח the Torah says 'on the first day there shall be a holy gathering.' There ראשון cannot mean the day before the חג, and no extra ו and ה explanation helps.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, there it is written: 'On the first day you shall have a holy gathering.' Does 'first' there mean 'earlier'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another problem. In a פסח verse about the holy gathering, ראשון obviously means the first day of יום טוב itself and not ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holy gathering and the ban on work belong to יום טוב, not to the day before, when work is allowed. This verse also says הָרִאשׁוֹן with the ה, yet it plainly means the first day of the חג. That weakens the claim that the ה in הראשון of תשביתו shows it means ערב פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, introducing an additional challenge
A holy gathering, meaning a day of יום טוב

phrases.english: And furthermore, there it is written:
"On the first day you shall have a holy gathering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא כג:ז, about פסח; רש"י counts it as the מקרא קודש of פסח.

phrases.english: Does 'first' there mean 'earlier'?!
phrases.notes: Clearly not. It is the first day of the חג.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge alongside step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of ראשון as 'the day before.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסח verse uses הָרִאשׁוֹן, with the ה, for the first day of יום טוב itself. So neither the ה nor the word ראשון can show that it means 'the day before.'

steps.title: The three times 'ראשון' appears are needed for a teaching about reward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. The times ראשון means 'first day of the חג' are written for the lesson of דבי רבי ישמעאל: as a reward for three ראשון, Israel earned three ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, those three times 'first' is written are needed for what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught. As a reward for the three 'firsts,' they earned three 'firsts': wiping out the offspring of עשו, the building of the בית המקדש, and the name of משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the ו and ה explanations and gives a new reason why the Torah says ראשון in those חג verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those uses of ראשון are written on purpose, to teach that keeping the מצוות of the ראשון days earns three things called ראשון. Since they have their own special purpose, they cannot prove what ראשון normally means. That leaves the reading of ראשון in תשביתו as 'the day before' in place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for, meaning it serves another purpose
The school of רבי ישמעאל, which taught a ברייתא
To cut off or wipe out

steps.whatToRemember: The ראשון in the חג verses is not proof against reading 'earlier.' Those words are there to teach the reward of three ראשון.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say that ראשון in those verses means 'earlier.' It says those words are written for a special lesson, so they cannot be used to prove the plain meaning elsewhere.

phrases.english: Rather, those three times 'first' is written

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: are needed for what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught.
As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
As a reward for three 'firsts,'
they merited three 'firsts':
to wipe out the offspring of עשו,
to the building of the בית המקדש,
and to the name of משיח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה רִאשׁוֹן מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers steps 20 and 21 by replacing the ו and ה explanations with a new purpose for the word ראשון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the challenging words a separate purpose (a דרשה about reward).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ראשון in the חג verses shows that ראשון means 'first day of the חג,' or must be explained through extra letters.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those ראשון words are written for the reward teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל, so the reading of תשביתו's ראשון as 'earlier' stands.

steps.title: Verses showing each reward is called 'ראשון'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק for each reward showing that it is called ראשון: עשו, the בית המקדש, and משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wiping out עשו's offspring, as it is written: 'The first came out red, all of him like a hairy coat.' The building of the בית המקדש, as it is written: 'Throne of glory, on high from the first, the place of our Sanctuary.' The name of משיח, as it is written: 'First to Zion, behold, here they are.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves that each of the three rewards is linked to the word ראשון in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עשו is called הראשון because he was born first, so his downfall is a 'ראשון' reward. The בית המקדש is called מראשון, existing from the beginning. משיח is the ראשון לציון, the first to bring good news to Zion.

phrases.english: To wipe out the offspring of עשו, as it is written:
"And the first came out red,
all of him like a hairy coat."
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:25

phrases.english: And to the building of the בית המקדש, as it is written:
"Throne of glory, on high from the first,
the place of our Sanctuary."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 17:12

phrases.english: And to the name of משיח, as it is written:
"First to Zion, behold, here they are."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 41:27

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוקים behind each of the three rewards listed in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That each of the three rewards is called ראשון.

steps.title: רבא's different source: no קרבן פסח while חמץ exists
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns the איסור חמץ from midday on the 14th from a different פסוק. Do not slaughter the קרבן פסח while חמץ still exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: from here: 'You shall not slaughter the blood of My offering over חמץ.' Do not slaughter the פסח while חמץ still exists.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a brand-new source, separate from the ראשון discussion, for why חמץ must be gone by midday on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח is slaughtered in the afternoon of the 14th. The Torah forbids slaughtering it 'על חמץ,' which רבא reads as 'while חמץ is still around.' So חמץ must already be gone by the time the קרבן פסח may be slaughtered, which is from midday.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, introducing a different source
My offering, here the קרבן פסח

steps.whatToRemember: רבא derives the deadline for removing חמץ from the time of slaughtering the קרבן פסח, not from the word ראשון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the איסור חמץ on ערב פסח directly to the time of the קרבן פסח, which begins at midday.

phrases.english: רבא said: from here:
"You shall not slaughter the blood of My offering over חמץ"
phrases.notes: שמות 34:25

phrases.english: do not slaughter the פסח
while חמץ still exists.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ראשון derivation and gives an independent source for the same law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ must be removed before the time for slaughtering the קרבן פסח, from the פסוק 'לא תשחט על חמץ דם זבחי.'

steps.title: Maybe each person only needs to be rid of חמץ when he slaughters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading. Perhaps 'do not slaughter while חמץ exists' is a personal rule for each person at the moment he slaughters, not a fixed time for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: each and every person, at the moment he slaughters his own קרבן פסח, must have no חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof from step 24. It suggests the פסוק might not set a fixed time at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא used the פסוק to show that חמץ is forbidden from midday on the 14th. The challenge is that people slaughter at different times, so the rule might apply to each person only at his own moment of שחיטה. If so, the פסוק does not prove a single starting time for the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And say instead': introduces another possible reading

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא: כָּל חַד וְחַד כִּי שָׁחֵיט!
phrases.english: But say: each and every one, when he slaughters!
phrases.notes: The rule would be tied to the moment each person slaughters, not to a fixed clock time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: כָּל חַד וְחַד כִּי שָׁחֵיט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's derivation in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that 'לא תשחט על חמץ' sets a fixed time for the איסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could describe a personal moment (when each person slaughters) rather than one shared time, so it would not prove that the איסור starts at midday for everyone.

steps.title: The Torah means the set time of slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the Torah is referring to the time period when the פסח may be slaughtered, which starts after midday. It is not referring to each person's own act.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One (the Torah) spoke about the time of slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק points to the official time for slaughtering the פסח, not to each person's private moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח may be slaughtered starting after midday on the 14th. The פסוק means that from that time on, חמץ may not exist, whether or not a particular person has slaughtered yet. That gives one fixed starting point for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: The time period for slaughtering (from after midday on the 14th)

phrases.english: The Merciful One spoke of the time of slaughtering.
phrases.notes: The פסוק defines a time, not a personal act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the פסוק refers to a time period, not an individual act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each person must be rid of חמץ only when he personally slaughters.
steps.terutzMaskana: From the general time of שחיטה (after midday on the 14th), חמץ is forbidden for everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא: רבי ישמעאל uses the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'on the first day you shall remove leaven' means the day before יום טוב. רבי ישמעאל proves this from 'do not slaughter My offering over חמץ', the same פסוק רבא used.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. 'But on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses' means from the day before יום טוב. Or perhaps it means only on יום טוב itself? So the פסוק says: 'Do not slaughter the blood of My offering over חמץ'. This means do not slaughter the פסח while חמץ still exists. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבא's teaching from step 24. רבי ישמעאל learns the same thing from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא raises a possible reading: the מצוה to remove חמץ might apply only on יום טוב itself. רבי ישמעאל rejects that reading with 'לא תשחט על חמץ'. Since the פסח is slaughtered on the 14th, חמץ must already be gone then, so 'the first day' must mean the 14th.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A ברייתא also teaches this': brings support for the previous statement
You shall remove / get rid of
The day before the יום טוב (here, the 14th of ניסן)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'הראשון' (the first) means the day BEFORE the חג, the 14th, not the first day of פסח. That is the whole point of this section.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a ברייתא):
"But on the first day
you shall remove leaven from your houses":
from the day before יום טוב.
phrases.notes: This is the conclusion the ברייתא is aiming for.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב עַצְמוֹ?
phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only on יום טוב itself?
phrases.notes: A possible reading that the ברייתא will reject.

phrases.english: The פסוק teaches:
"Do not slaughter the blood of My offering over חמץ":
Do not slaughter the פסח
while חמץ still exists,
these are the words of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings ברייתא support for רבא's derivation in step 24
steps.raayaObject: רבא's derivation that חמץ is forbidden from the time of שחיטת הפסח on the 14th
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי ישמעאל uses 'לא תשחט על חמץ דם זבחי'

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: you cannot burn חמץ on יום טוב, so the מצוה must be the day before
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says no extra פסוק is needed. Kindling a fire is a main category of forbidden work, and work is forbidden on יום טוב. So the burning of חמץ must happen on ערב יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: that proof is not needed. The Torah says 'But on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses', and it is written 'You shall do no work'. And we find that kindling a fire is a main category of work.
steps.whatsHappening: In the same ברייתא, רבי עקיבא gives a different proof that 'the first day' means the 14th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing חמץ is done by burning it, which requires kindling a fire. On יום טוב, fire is allowed only for food needs, and burning חמץ is not a food need. So 'the first day' cannot mean יום טוב and must mean the day before.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (that proof is unnecessary)
A main category of forbidden work

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: it is not needed,
for it says:
"But on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses,"
and it is written: "You shall do no work,"
and we have found that kindling a fire
is a main category of work.
phrases.notes: So burning חמץ on יום טוב would be forbidden. The removal must happen on the 14th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different proof for the same conclusion as רבי ישמעאל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since burning is forbidden work on יום טוב, the מצוה of removing חמץ must be done on ערב יום טוב.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the word 'אך' splits the day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי also says no extra proof is needed. The word 'אך' (but/only) divides the 14th into two halves. חמץ is allowed in the morning and forbidden after midday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: that proof is not needed. The Torah says 'But on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses', meaning from the day before יום טוב. Or perhaps it means on יום טוב? So the פסוק says 'אך', which divides.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a third proof that the מצוה applies on the 14th, this time from the word 'אך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אך' is a limiting word, so it 'divides' the day: only part of the 14th is included. A split day only makes sense for the 14th, when the איסור starts at midday. On יום טוב, חמץ is forbidden the whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But / only': a limiting word that divides

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says: it is not needed,
for it says:
"But on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses":
from the day before יום טוב.
Or perhaps it is only on יום טוב?
The פסוק says "אך": it divided.
phrases.notes: Half the day חמץ is allowed and half the day it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third proof for the same conclusion, alongside רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אך' divides the 14th: חמץ is permitted before midday and forbidden after it.
steps.whatToRemember: Three proofs that 'the first day' of removing חמץ is the 14th: רבי ישמעאל (do not slaughter the פסח over חמץ), רבי עקיבא (you cannot burn on יום טוב), and רבי יוסי ('אך' splits the day).

steps.title: How could anyone think חמץ is allowed on יום טוב itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's suggestion that the מצוה might apply on יום טוב itself. חמץ is obviously forbidden on יום טוב, since the פסוקים link removing leaven to not eating חמץ, and not eating חמץ to eating מצה. רבא is introduced to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the פסוק meant יום טוב itself, would חמץ be allowed until then? Removing leaven is linked to eating חמץ, and eating חמץ is linked to eating מצה! רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the starting idea in the ברייתא ('or perhaps it is on יום טוב itself'). It then sets up רבא's answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If removal began only on יום טוב, חמץ would be permitted for part of יום טוב. But the Torah links removal to the איסור of eating חמץ, and that איסור to the מצוה of מצה, which starts at night. So חמץ is forbidden the whole יום טוב, and the ברייתא's possible reading seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: Was linked / compared (a היקש between two פסוקים)
Eating מצה (a מצוה from the night of the 15th)

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בְּיוֹם טוֹב עַצְמוֹ, מִי שְׁרֵי?
phrases.english: And if it were on יום טוב itself, is חמץ permitted?
phrases.notes: He's not really asking. Of course it is not!

phrases.english: But removing leaven was linked
to the איסור of eating חמץ,
and eating חמץ to eating מצה!
phrases.notes: מצה is eaten from the night of the 15th, so חמץ is forbidden from then. Removal cannot start later than that.

phrases.english: רבא said:
phrases.notes: This only introduces רבא's answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בְּיוֹם טוֹב עַצְמוֹ, מִי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the possible reading ('או אינו אלא ביום טוב') in the ברייתא of steps 27–29
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's suggestion that the מצוה of removing חמץ might apply only on יום טוב itself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Through the links, removing leaven is tied to the איסור of eating חמץ, which is tied to the מצוה of מצה from the night of the 15th. So חמץ is forbidden all of יום טוב, and removal starting during יום טוב makes no sense.
